Source   Edit  

The memory of the VM. All VM values live in memory that is owned by the VM and that is tracked as a set of regions. Every access through a pointer that the VM cannot prove to be valid is checked against the regions so that a bogus cast produces a VM error instead of crashing the compiler.

There are different kinds of regions:

  • the VM stack: frames are bump allocated from stack segments.
  • the globals segment: compile-time globals; never freed.
  • the const segment: constant data (string literals, const values); read-only and never freed.
  • heap chunks: blocks for new, string and seq payloads, alloc.
  • big blocks: heap blocks too large for a chunk get a region of their own.
  • foreign regions: memory handed to the VM by FFI calls.

Regions never move, so addresses are stable and the VM can use real host pointers for ptr, ref, var etc.

NimNode and typedesc values are represented by 32 bit handles: indexes into tables of this module. Handle 0 always means nil. Procs are represented by addresses within proc regions: these addresses are unique, so they can be told apart from integers that are cast to a proc type, yet they cannot be read or written.
